messages.text: Is current tokenizer large because it supports all language? Would it be a bottleneck in keeping model small? Should we just focus on English?

messages.author: Antigravity (Tutor)
messages.text: Yes, absolutely! The 100,262 token vocabulary consumes 77.0M parameters—over 50.6% of our entire 152M model budget. By pruning to a specialized 16k Python+English tokenizer, we reclaim 64.4M parameters, allowing us to increase Transformer depth from 12 to 20+ layers under the exact same parameter budget.

messages.author: Antigravity (Tutor)
messages.text: Mechanically it works via 256 byte-fallback (zero crashes), but causes severe token inflation (literature words chopped into 4-5 pieces, shrinking effective context). Once a model is trained, its tokenizer is permanently frozen to its embedding matrix. The frontier fix: train upfront on an 80/20 Code + Technical English blend!

messages.author: Antigravity (Tutor)
messages.text: 1) Code needs more tokens (80/20) because Python syntax is unforgiving whereas English is flexible; 2) Mix is decided via DoReMi pilot ablations tracing the Pareto frontier; 3) Misspellings are handled via 3-tier subword fallback (['pal', 'in', 'drom']) where semantic vectors overlap with correct words.

messages.author: Antigravity (Tutor)
messages.text: Spot on! ~200MB provides ~50M-70M characters, ensuring Zipf's law distribution populates all 16k-32k merges with statistically robust patterns while preventing one-off variables from polluting the vocabulary. Running code through ruff/black standardizes 4-space indentation (hitting our multi-space indentation token optimization 100% of the time) and collapses stylistic noise.
